strategies.name: Time-series momentum
strategies.thesis: Assets that rose over the look-back keep rising: long when price > its N-bar-ago level, short otherwise (Moskowitz–Ooi–Pedersen).
strategies.origin: Classic academic TSMOM (Moskowitz, Ooi, Pedersen). FMC ships a single-asset, vol-scaled version.
strategies.intuition: Markets trend more often than a coin flip at multi-week horizons. You do not predict the next tick — you align with the last persistent move and cut size when volatility spikes.
strategies.schematic:
<svg viewBox="0 0 640 280" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" role="img" aria-label="Time-series momentum schematic">
  <rect width="640" height="280" fill="#f8f9fc"/>
  <text x="24" y="28" fill="#4f46e5" font-family="ui-sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" letter-spacing="2">SCHEMATIC · TSMOM</text>
  <polyline points="40,200 120,180 200,140 280,150 360,90 440,100 520,60 600,70" fill="none" stroke="#0b1020" stroke-width="2.5"/>
  <line x1="200" y1="40" x2="200" y2="240" stroke="#8b91ab" stroke-dasharray="4 4"/>
  <text x="208" y="54" fill="#8b91ab" font-size="11" font-family="monospace">t−N</text>
  <line x1="520" y1="40" x2="520" y2="240" stroke="#4f46e5" stroke-dasharray="4 4"/>
  <text x="528" y="54" fill="#4f46e5" font-size="11" font-family="monospace">now</text>
  <path d="M210 150 L500 75" stroke="#059669" stroke-width="2" marker-end="url(#a)"/>
  <defs><marker id="a" markerWidth="8" markerHeight="8" refX="6" refY="3" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L6,3 L0,6 Z" fill="#059669"/></marker></defs>
  <rect x="40" y="230" width="14" height="14" fill="#059669"/><text x="62" y="241" font-size="12" fill="#0b1020">Long if P_now > P_t−N</text>
  <rect x="280" y="230" width="14" height="14" fill="#e11d48"/><text x="302" y="241" font-size="12" fill="#0b1020">Short otherwise · size ∝ 1/σ</text>
</svg>
steps: Pick a liquid symbol (indices, futures, majors, liquid crypto).
Choose look-back N (FMC default 60 bars on your active timeframe).
Compute the raw signal: sign(close − close[N bars ago]).
Estimate realised volatility (e.g. 20-bar stdev of returns).
Scale position so risk per bar is roughly constant (target ≈ 1% move).
Enter on the next bar open after the signal flips; trail or flip on opposite signal.
Backtest in the lxScript editor, then paper-trade with the FMC bot before any live capital.
rules: Long when close > close[N]; short when close < close[N].
Position size = clamp(target_vol / realised_vol, 0 … 1.0).
No trade until look-back is warm (first N bars flat).
Optional: skip entries in high_vol regime from the AGI Regime Classifier.
best_for: Traders who hate constant notional sizing
avoid_when: News-spike days without a vol filter
Illiquid names where gaps destroy the sign signal
risks: Crowded after long trends → sharp reversals
Underestimates gap risk on crypto weekends

strategies.name: Bollinger mean reversion
strategies.thesis: Closes beyond ±2σ bands snap back toward the mean in range-bound regimes; fade the excursion, exit at the midline.
strategies.origin: Bollinger (1980s) + short-term reversal literature. FMC fades 2σ closes and exits at the 20-bar mean.
strategies.intuition: In quiet / mean-revert regimes, extremes are rental — price borrows from the mean and pays it back. You sell richness and buy cheapness, then leave when the rent is paid.
strategies.schematic:
<svg viewBox="0 0 640 280" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" role="img" aria-label="Bollinger mean reversion schematic">
  <rect width="640" height="280" fill="#f8f9fc"/>
  <text x="24" y="28" fill="#4f46e5" font-family="ui-sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" letter-spacing="2">SCHEMATIC · BOLLINGER FADE</text>
  <path d="M40,80 Q160,60 280,90 T520,70 T600,85" fill="none" stroke="#8b5cf6" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-dasharray="5 4"/>
  <path d="M40,200 Q160,220 280,190 T520,210 T600,195" fill="none" stroke="#8b5cf6" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-dasharray="5 4"/>
  <path d="M40,140 Q200,135 360,145 T600,140" fill="none" stroke="#4f46e5" stroke-width="2"/>
  <polyline points="40,150 100,145 160,155 220,120 280,160 340,90 400,150 460,170 520,130 580,148" fill="none" stroke="#0b1020" stroke-width="2.2"/>
  <circle cx="340" cy="90" r="7" fill="#e11d48"/><text x="354" y="86" font-size="11" fill="#e11d48" font-family="monospace">SHORT @ +2σ</text>
  <circle cx="400" cy="150" r="7" fill="#059669"/><text x="414" y="146" font-size="11" fill="#059669" font-family="monospace">COVER @ mid</text>
  <text x="40" y="250" font-size="12" fill="#4a5170">Upper / lower = mid ± 2·σ(20) · only trade when Regime = mean_revert / quiet</text>
</svg>
steps: Confirm FMC Regime Classifier is mean_revert or quiet (not high_vol / strong trend).
Plot 20-bar SMA (mid) and ±2σ bands.
Wait for a close outside the band (not just a wick).
Fade: short above upper, long below lower.
Exit when price returns to the midline (or stop beyond a 3σ extension).
One position at a time; no pyramiding into the fade.
Load the lxScript, backtest, then paper with journal tags “MR / Boll”.
rules: Entry: close > mid+2σ → short; close < mid−2σ → long.
Exit: cross back through mid (or time-stop after N bars).
Flat if ATR expands > 1.5× its 40-bar mean (vol break).
best_for: Indices after a vertical spike that stalls
risks: Catching a breakout disguised as a fade

strategies.name: Volatility-targeted trend
strategies.thesis: Hold the trend direction but size inversely to realised volatility so risk per bar is constant.
strategies.origin: Industry standard overlay on trend sleeves (risk parity / vol targeting literature).
strategies.intuition: The edge is often in the direction; the ruin is in the sizing. Same directional view, smaller size when the tape is loud.
strategies.schematic:
<svg viewBox="0 0 640 280" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" role="img" aria-label="Volatility targeting schematic">
  <rect width="640" height="280" fill="#f8f9fc"/>
  <text x="24" y="28" fill="#4f46e5" font-family="ui-sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" letter-spacing="2">SCHEMATIC · VOL TARGET</text>
  <text x="40" y="70" font-size="13" fill="#0b1020" font-weight="700">Direction = sign(EMA20 − EMA80)</text>
  <text x="40" y="100" font-size="13" fill="#0b1020" font-weight="700">Size = min(1.5, target / (σ20 / price))</text>
  <rect x="40" y="130" width="240" height="90" rx="12" fill="#eef0ff" stroke="#4f46e5"/>
  <text x="56" y="158" font-size="12" fill="#4f46e5">Low σ → larger size</text>
  <text x="56" y="182" font-size="12" fill="#4a5170">Quiet trend = lean in</text>
  <rect x="320" y="130" width="240" height="90" rx="12" fill="#ffe4e6" stroke="#e11d48"/>
  <text x="336" y="158" font-size="12" fill="#e11d48">High σ → cut size</text>
  <text x="336" y="182" font-size="12" fill="#4a5170">Same signal, less risk</text>
</svg>
steps: Compute fast EMA (20) and slow EMA (80).
Direction = sign(fast − slow).
Compute 20-bar return stdev / price.
Size = clamp(target / vol, 0 … 1.5).
Rebalance size when vol changes by >20%.
Combine with journal discipline score ≥ 55 before increasing the target.
rules: Never flip direction and double size on the same bar
Cap leverage at 1.5× even if vol collapses
Stand aside if Anomaly Sentinel = critical
best_for: Multi-asset desks that need comparable risk
avoid_when: Broker min size makes fractional sizing impossible

strategies.name: Session drift (overnight anomaly proxy)
strategies.thesis: Equity index returns concentrate in specific session segments; hold only during historically favourable hours.
strategies.origin: Overnight / close-to-open anomaly literature (Cooper, Cliff, Gulen and successors).
strategies.intuition: A large share of equity drift historically accrued outside the continuous cash session. FMC approximates that by holding only in a UTC hour window.
strategies.schematic:
<svg viewBox="0 0 640 280" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" role="img" aria-label="Session drift schematic">
  <rect width="640" height="280" fill="#f8f9fc"/>
  <text x="24" y="28" fill="#4f46e5" font-family="ui-sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" letter-spacing="2">SCHEMATIC · SESSION FILTER</text>
  <rect x="40" y="100" width="160" height="60" fill="#d1fae5" stroke="#059669"/><text x="70" y="135" font-size="12">HOLD 18–02 UTC</text>
  <rect x="200" y="100" width="360" height="60" fill="#eef0f6" stroke="#8b91ab"/><text x="320" y="135" font-size="12" fill="#4a5170">FLAT (cash session proxy)</text>
  <text x="40" y="200" font-size="12" fill="#4a5170">Tune the hour window to your market (US cash vs futures vs crypto 24/7).</text>
</svg>
steps: Decide which session anomaly you are targeting (US overnight, futures roll, etc.).
Map that to UTC hours on your bar timeframe.
Hold long only inside the window; flat otherwise (or hedge).
Disable around holidays / early closes.
Validate month-by-month — seasonality dies and revives.
rules: Position ∈ {0, 1} from hour filter only
No fade of the filter with discretion
Re-estimate window yearly
best_for: Traders who can hold through the close
risks: Regime change after structural market hours shifts
Gap risk into the hold window

strategies.name: RSI(2) pullback
strategies.thesis: Connors: buy deep short-term oversold (RSI2 < 10) when above the 200-bar mean; exit above RSI 65.
strategies.origin: Larry Connors’ RSI(2) mean-reversion playbook — widely studied in short-term equity / ETF research.
strategies.intuition: In an uptrend (price above the long mean), panic is temporary. RSI(2) hits absurdly low levels that rarely persist; you buy the flush and sell the snap-back.
strategies.schematic:
<svg viewBox="0 0 640 280" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" role="img" aria-label="RSI2 pullback schematic">
  <rect width="640" height="280" fill="#f8f9fc"/>
  <text x="24" y="28" fill="#4f46e5" font-family="ui-sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" letter-spacing="2">SCHEMATIC · RSI(2) CONNORS</text>
  <text x="40" y="58" font-size="12" fill="#4a5170">Price pane</text>
  <polyline points="40,110 120,100 200,85 280,95 360,70 440,88 520,60 600,55" fill="none" stroke="#0b1020" stroke-width="2"/>
  <path d="M40,120 Q200,125 400,115 T600,118" fill="none" stroke="#8b5cf6" stroke-dasharray="4 3"/>
  <text x="480" y="112" font-size="10" fill="#8b5cf6" font-family="monospace">SMA200</text>
  <circle cx="280" cy="95" r="6" fill="#059669"/><text x="292" y="90" font-size="11" fill="#059669">BUY</text>
  <text x="40" y="160" font-size="12" fill="#4a5170">RSI(2) pane</text>
  <line x1="40" y1="190" x2="600" y2="190" stroke="#e11d48" stroke-dasharray="3 3"/><text x="605" y="194" font-size="10" fill="#e11d48">10</text>
  <line x1="40" y1="210" x2="600" y2="210" stroke="#059669" stroke-dasharray="3 3"/><text x="605" y="214" font-size="10" fill="#059669">65</text>
  <polyline points="40,200 120,195 200,185 280,250 360,200 440,175 520,168 600,170" fill="none" stroke="#4f46e5" stroke-width="2"/>
  <circle cx="280" cy="250" r="5" fill="#059669"/><circle cx="440" cy="175" r="5" fill="#e11d48"/>
  <text x="40" y="268" font-size="11" fill="#4a5170">Entry: price > SMA200 AND RSI2 < 10 · Exit: RSI2 > 65</text>
</svg>
steps: Confirm the market is in a longer-term uptrend: close above the 200-bar SMA (or half-sample SMA if the tape is shorter).
Plot RSI with length 2 on a lower pane.
Wait for RSI(2) to print below 10 (deep short-term oversold).
Enter long on the next bar; do not chase if price already ripped back above the mean.
Exit when RSI(2) crosses above 65 (Connors-style), or on a close back under the 200-SMA (trend break).
Optional stop: prior swing low or 1.5× ATR — Connors often used time/RSI exits more than tight stops.
Open Study → Load & backtest the built-in script → review Live Lens → journal the paper trades.
rules: Long only (this FMC version does not short RSI(2) > 90 in downtrends).
Filter: close > SMA200.
Entry: RSI2 < 10.
Exit: RSI2 > 65.
One unit; no averaging down more than once.
best_for: Traders who already trust the primary uptrend
avoid_when: Earnings / binary events on single names
High_vol regime with Anomaly Sentinel critical
risks: Buying a trend change disguised as a pullback
Clusters of losses if the uptrend is dying

strategies.name: Donchian channel breakout
strategies.thesis: Turtle-style: buy 20-bar highs, sell 20-bar lows, exit on the opposite 10-bar extreme.
strategies.origin: Donchian channels / Turtle Traders — the purest breakout template in quant trend-following.
strategies.intuition: When price makes a new N-bar high, something informed (or crowded) is pushing. You join and leave when the move fails a shorter channel.
strategies.schematic:
<svg viewBox="0 0 640 280" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" role="img" aria-label="Donchian breakout schematic">
  <rect width="640" height="280" fill="#f8f9fc"/>
  <text x="24" y="28" fill="#4f46e5" font-family="ui-sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" letter-spacing="2">SCHEMATIC · DONCHIAN 20/10</text>
  <path d="M40,100 H600" stroke="#059669" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/><text x="500" y="92" font-size="11" fill="#059669">20-bar high</text>
  <path d="M40,200 H600" stroke="#e11d48" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/><text x="500" y="220" font-size="11" fill="#e11d48">20-bar low</text>
  <polyline points="40,160 100,150 160,155 220,140 280,130 340,95 400,110 460,100 520,120" fill="none" stroke="#0b1020" stroke-width="2.4"/>
  <circle cx="340" cy="95" r="7" fill="#059669"/><text x="354" y="88" font-size="11" fill="#059669">BUY break</text>
  <path d="M400,130 H560" stroke="#8b91ab" stroke-dasharray="3 3"/><text x="430" y="148" font-size="10" fill="#8b91ab">exit on 10-bar low</text>
</svg>
steps: Compute 20-bar highest high and lowest low.
Long when close breaks above prior 20-bar high; short on break of prior 20-bar low.
Exit long on close below prior 10-bar low (symmetric for shorts).
Use vol targeting or ATR stops if your venue gaps.
Expect many small losses and a few large wins — do not “improve” by skipping breakouts.
rules: Entry channel 20
Exit channel 10
Always in (long or short) unless you add a filter
Optional: skip if inside Bollinger mid range
best_for: Systematic traders OK with low win rate
avoid_when: Tight sideways years without a chop filter

strategies.name: VWAP reversion
strategies.thesis: Institutions benchmark to VWAP; stretched deviations (>1.5σ) revert as execution algos lean against them.
strategies.origin: Market microstructure / execution benchmarking. FMC fades 1.5σ deviations from session VWAP.
strategies.intuition: When price is far from VWAP, passive execution flow often works back toward it. You fade the stretch and exit near VWAP.
strategies.schematic:
<svg viewBox="0 0 640 280" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" role="img" aria-label="VWAP reversion schematic">
  <rect width="640" height="280" fill="#f8f9fc"/>
  <text x="24" y="28" fill="#4f46e5" font-family="ui-sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" letter-spacing="2">SCHEMATIC · VWAP FADE</text>
  <path d="M40,150 Q200,145 360,155 T600,150" fill="none" stroke="#4f46e5" stroke-width="2.5"/>
  <text x="520" y="140" font-size="11" fill="#4f46e5" font-family="monospace">VWAP</text>
  <path d="M40,110 Q200,105 360,115 T600,110" fill="none" stroke="#8b5cf6" stroke-dasharray="4 3"/>
  <path d="M40,190 Q200,185 360,195 T600,190" fill="none" stroke="#8b5cf6" stroke-dasharray="4 3"/>
  <polyline points="40,148 120,140 200,160 280,100 360,170 440,130 520,155" fill="none" stroke="#0b1020" stroke-width="2"/>
  <circle cx="280" cy="100" r="6" fill="#e11d48"/><text x="292" y="96" font-size="11" fill="#e11d48">fade +1.5σ</text>
  <circle cx="360" cy="170" r="6" fill="#059669"/><text x="374" y="186" font-size="11" fill="#059669">exit ~ VWAP</text>
</svg>
steps: Use intraday bars (1m–15m) so VWAP is meaningful.
Compute session VWAP and rolling σ of (price − VWAP).
Short when deviation > +1.5σ; long when < −1.5σ.
Exit when |deviation| < 0.2σ (back to value).
Flat into the cash close if you cannot hold overnight.
rules: No fade in the first 15 minutes if open auction is wild
Cut if deviation expands to 3σ against you
One fade at a time
avoid_when: Trend days where VWAP is a magnet then a runway

strategies.name: Bear-market hedge overlay
strategies.thesis: Cut exposure when price is under the 200-bar mean and realised vol is expanding; re-enter when both normalise.
strategies.origin: Bear-market / defensive overlay playbooks — capital preservation first.
strategies.intuition: Most careers die in drawdowns, not in missed rallies. When trend and vol both say danger, shrink beta.
strategies.schematic:
<svg viewBox="0 0 640 280" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" role="img" aria-label="Bear hedge schematic">
  <rect width="640" height="280" fill="#f8f9fc"/>
  <text x="24" y="28" fill="#4f46e5" font-family="ui-sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" letter-spacing="2">SCHEMATIC · DEFENSIVE OVERLAY</text>
  <polyline points="40,80 160,90 280,100 400,160 520,200 600,210" fill="none" stroke="#0b1020" stroke-width="2.4"/>
  <path d="M40,120 Q300,125 600,130" fill="none" stroke="#8b5cf6" stroke-dasharray="5 4"/>
  <rect x="360" y="150" width="200" height="70" rx="10" fill="#ffe4e6" stroke="#e11d48"/>
  <text x="376" y="180" font-size="12" fill="#e11d48">Price < SMA200</text>
  <text x="376" y="200" font-size="12" fill="#e11d48">σ rising → cut / hedge</text>
</svg>
steps: Run this as an overlay on your core long sleeve — not as a standalone alpha.
If close < SMA200 AND short vol > 1.3× slow vol → reduce to 0 or small short hedge (−0.5).
If close > SMA200 AND vol calm → full long risk (1.0).
Re-risk slowly after the all-clear (two consecutive calm weeks).
Log every de-risk event in the journal with mood tag.
rules: Overlay, not hero trade
Never 3× reverse into a crash
Re-entry rules written in advance
avoid_when: You need maximum CAGR and accept 50% DD

strategies.name: Crypto momentum (skip-last-bars)
strategies.thesis: 1–4 week momentum persists in crypto; skip the most recent bars to dodge short-term reversal.
strategies.origin: Crypto momentum research syntheses — formation lag / skip-period is the practical trick.
strategies.intuition: Crypto trends, but the last day is noise and liquidation theater. Measure momentum ending a few bars ago.
strategies.schematic:
<svg viewBox="0 0 640 280" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" role="img" aria-label="Crypto momentum schematic">
  <rect width="640" height="280" fill="#f8f9fc"/>
  <text x="24" y="28" fill="#4f46e5" font-family="ui-sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" letter-spacing="2">SCHEMATIC · SKIP-PERIOD MOM</text>
  <rect x="80" y="100" width="280" height="50" fill="#eef0ff" stroke="#4f46e5"/><text x="120" y="130" font-size="12">Formation window</text>
  <rect x="360" y="100" width="80" height="50" fill="#ffe4e6" stroke="#e11d48"/><text x="372" y="130" font-size="12">SKIP</text>
  <rect x="440" y="100" width="100" height="50" fill="#d1fae5" stroke="#059669"/><text x="460" y="130" font-size="12">NOW</text>
  <text x="80" y="200" font-size="12" fill="#4a5170">Signal = price[t−skip] / price[t−look−skip] − 1</text>
</svg>
steps: Use BTC/ETH or a liquid perpetual.
Set look ≈ 4 weeks of bars; skip ≈ 2 bars (or 1–3 days).
Long if formation return > 0; reduce short if < 0 (FMC uses −0.5).
Vol-target the sleeve; funding rates can eat carry.
Stand down around major network events / ETF decisions if you cannot model them.
rules: Skip period mandatory
No leverage > venue maintenance margin comfort
Weekend gaps — size down
best_for: Momentum believers who hate last-tick noise

strategies.name: Pairs / spread z-score
strategies.thesis: Trade the z-score of a spread vs its slow mean; enter ±2, exit near 0. FMC uses price vs its own slow mean as a single-asset teaching proxy.
strategies.origin: Classic pairs / stat-arb (Gatev et al. and industry practice). Teaching form here is residual z-score.
strategies.intuition: When a spread is statistically stretched, expect convergence — if the relationship still exists. Always ask: did the cointegration break?
strategies.schematic:
<svg viewBox="0 0 640 280" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" role="img" aria-label="Pairs z-score schematic">
  <rect width="640" height="280" fill="#f8f9fc"/>
  <text x="24" y="28" fill="#4f46e5" font-family="ui-sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" letter-spacing="2">SCHEMATIC · Z-SCORE SPREAD</text>
  <line x1="40" y1="140" x2="600" y2="140" stroke="#8b91ab"/>
  <line x1="40" y1="80" x2="600" y2="80" stroke="#e11d48" stroke-dasharray="4 3"/><text x="605" y="84" font-size="10" fill="#e11d48">+2</text>
  <line x1="40" y1="200" x2="600" y2="200" stroke="#059669" stroke-dasharray="4 3"/><text x="605" y="204" font-size="10" fill="#059669">−2</text>
  <polyline points="40,140 100,130 160,150 220,90 280,160 340,210 400,150 460,135 520,145" fill="none" stroke="#4f46e5" stroke-width="2.2"/>
  <circle cx="220" cy="90" r="6" fill="#e11d48"/><text x="232" y="86" font-size="11">short spread</text>
  <circle cx="340" cy="210" r="6" fill="#059669"/><text x="352" y="226" font-size="11">long spread</text>
</svg>
steps: For true pairs: choose cointegrated candidates (not just correlated).
Build spread = A − βB (or log ratio); FMC demo uses price − SMA60.
Z = (spread − mean) / σ.
Short spread at z > 2; long at z < −2; flat at |z| < 0.25.
Hard stop if |z| > 4 (relationship break).
Paper only until you can explain why the pair should mean-revert.
rules: Stop on structural break
Equal risk legs when trading two names
No pairs without a thesis

// Pillars: kill zone, rule of 3, overbalance bar, RSI extreme — see STRATEGY_SPEC in mmc_confluence_strike.py
strategies.origin: Mens Mercatus Geometric Sniper dossier, empirically calibrated on FMC research harness.
strategies.intuition: You do not chase breakouts. You wait for liquidity hours, exhaustion cues, and a deep 0.618 retracement inside the session box — then scalp a small slice of the range with the trail at your back.
strategies.schematic:
